text:
alex: Morning — hitting a weird 401 when setting Basic auth from env var. Customer key contains an emoji and some non-ascii. If I manually paste the header it works. From Node/our SDK using `Authorization: Basic <base64>` it fails. Also: what is the least-disruptive way to rotate keys (add secondary key + cutover) for clients using Basic auth?

pat: Two quick things to check first: hidden chars/newlines and remembering the trailing colon in Basic auth (password empty). If you base64 the wrong bytes you'll get a different header.

pat: Bash example that always works (no newline):
```bash
# include trailing colon for empty password
echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64 -w0
# header: Authorization: Basic <output>
```

pat: If on macOS (no -w):
```bash
echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64
```

maria: If the key has Unicode or emoji, make sure you encode UTF-8 bytes, not some locale/terminal-decoded text. In Node: 
```js
const header = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':', 'utf8').toString('base64')
// set header exactly like this
```

kevin: Also check for CRLF/BOM/trailing newline. Common culprits: editors adding newline, CI secrets with \n, or copying from docs. Quick checks: `cat -v` or `xxd` to see hidden bytes.

kevin: Examples:
```bash
# show special chars/newline markers
printf "%s" "$API_KEY" | xxd -p -c 256
# or show line endings
cat -A secret.txt
```

maria: PowerShell (UTF-8 safe):
```powershell
$k = $env:API_KEY + ':'
[Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($k))
# then Authorization: Basic <that>
```

alex: Good call — I found a trailing CRLF in the secret created by a portal. Removed newline and now Node works. Thanks!

pat: For rotation: create a secondary key and accept both keys server-side during rollout. Eg: keep whitelist of active key ids and allow either key for a short period, then revoke the old one. If clients only send raw Basic, consider encouraging Key-ID header or API-Key header so you can rotate without guessing which key was used (and avoid base64 confusion).

maria: We also do this at Redwood: issue key pairs with metadata (key-id) and prefer `Authorization: Basic <b64>` only for backward compatibility. New SDKs send `x-api-key-id: <id>` and `Authorization: Basic <b64>` — server validates id first so rotation is easy.

kevin: Quick curl sanity test you can run from any env: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"$API_KEY:\" | base64 -w0)" https://api.example.com/v1/_health
```
If you get 401 locally but the pasted header works, compare `echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64` output vs the header you pasted.

alex: one more weird streaming note — when using our Node streaming client I saw intermittent 400s when the auth header had multibyte chars before base64ing. Fixed by ensuring `Buffer.from(..., 'utf8')` and setting the header with a plain string (not a Buffer object).

ci-bot: deploy status: all tests passed for auth-header-fix branch :white_check_mark:

alex: awesome, will add a short devex snippet to the quickstart about emoji/unicode keys + rotation checklist. Thanks all :tada:
